study.question: Can a low-rank common-context map preserve the semantic sparse incumbent click AUC and reduce measured prediction cost when further context splitting and nonlinear-width reduction both failed?
study.hypothesis: The unsuccessful context split may remove useful context access across the two semantic branches, rather than demonstrate that every independent context coefficient is necessary. A shared low-rank context map feeding all112 buy channels may retain sufficient context-mediated auxiliary learning while compressing redundant coefficients. This is unverified: whole-buy-affine rank73 previously underperformed, so localizing rank reduction to context alone is a discriminating follow-up, not a transfer assumption. Rank35 nearly matches the last context-split parameter budget; rank48 tests a less restrictive dose. Buy gradients into shared context may change click learning even though the click head is untouched.

nearest_work.difference: Archived primary text lines56-100 and135-189 inspected. Inherit target-dependent history weighting and Dice via local adaptation; current intervention is only the common-context block of the buy readout after inherited compression. No DIN reproduction or originality claim.

Pinned benchmark source lines190-239 inspected: LowRankLinear uses down/up linear projections for flattened-token Q/K/V. The two-linear rank constraint is established prior machinery. Here factor only the112x192 common-context block of an already sparse buy first affine; preserve separate local target/history weights, with SVD initialization from a fresh untrained parent. This is no HiFormer implementation or new low-rank primitive.

Resolved original link; detailed original text unavailable through authorized source, fallback benchmark description and source read separately. Original-method equivalence and priority remain unverified.

Cached section2.3 inspected as benchmark-authored method descriptions, including heterogeneous/token interaction and low-rank token mixing; not a primary audit of the original fifteen methods. Current local study replaces neither history aggregation nor token interaction.

Proposed rank constraint applies only to context coefficients, leaving semantic local maps unrestricted.

study.proposed_difference: After the entire parent initialization, replace only the buy packed first affine. Fused reference is an exact source-path no-op. Separate dense control stores W_context[112,192] plus unchanged local weights[56,96] and[56,112], and sums the common context projection with concatenated local branches. Following Dice/second affine/readout and all other modules stay intact. No full context matrix/backing storage/cache survives in rank variants. All train/eval calls use the declared operator; BF16 reassociation can differ even in separate dense control.

Freeze cost gate: a useful candidate must have fewer host-measured dense parameters and at least1% lower model-only p50 batch latency than contemporaneous fused reference, with p95 no more than1% worse. falsifiers: Both ranks reproducibly fail the original-entry or incumbent preservation gates: reject utility of this bounded implementation; this does not prove all context rank is necessary.

A rank that preserves AUC but misses measured prediction-cost gate is a capacity result only, not a demonstrated efficiency improvement. Extra GEMMs/gathers/additions or rank35 hardware alignment may erase analytic savings.
Dense separated control changes AUC comparably to rank variants, or an apparent gain disappears under paired repetition: rank-specific explanation remains unsupported.
Rank35 matches split/width64 quality despite preserving global context access: no support for broad-access benefit at that budget; rank48-only success limits the compression dose claim.
Nonfinite outputs/gradients, altered ownership/masks, wrong storage counts, label access or failed reference reproduction invalidate the affected comparison; retain failed cost/receipt.
